1	# kaggle-code-agent Milestones
2	
3	Status: M6 done, M7 in planning  
4	Created: 2026-05-16  
5	Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform
6	
7	## Product thesis
8	
9	`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.
10	
11	Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
12	Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.
13	
14	The platform should help a human user:
15	
16	- discuss ideas and strategies;
17	- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
18	- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
19	- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
20	- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
21	- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.
22	
23	## Source of truth
24	
25	**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**
26	
27	All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.
28	
29	Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.
30	
31	## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"
32	
33	This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.
34	
35	### 1. Platform-development coding agents
36	
37	These are external AI tools used to build this repository.
38	
39	Examples:
40	
41	- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
42	- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
43	- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.
44	
45	Role:
46	
47	- write and review this product's source code;
48	- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
49	- run local tests and CI repair loops;
50	- open branches/PRs under human supervision.
51	
52	Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.
53	
54	### 2. Runtime competition code agents
55	
56	These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.
57	
58	Initial runtime direction:
59	
60	- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
61	- isolated workspace/container per job;
62	- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
63	- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
64	- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.
65	
66	Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.

69

76	  - discussion/research/analysis records

85	  - sandboxed execution and evaluation

88	  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs

95	
96	- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
97	- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
98	- Main branch remains stable and protected.
99	- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.

335	## M6: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓ done
336	
337	Goal: harden the M3–M5 worker with an independent reviewer agent, end-to-end
338	OpenTelemetry tracing, and a local-model layer that routes log-triage /
339	summarisation jobs to user-owned GPU hosts before paying for cloud tokens.
340	
341	Planned capabilities:
342	
343	- Reviewer agent (sync mode) fires before high-stakes ops
344	  (`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
345	  `delete_artifact`). Verdict `approve | reject | abstain` lands in a new
346	  `agent_reviews` table; `approve` satisfies the matching approval gate
347	  without human intervention, `reject` escalates (default) or fails the
348	  job, `abstain` falls through to the existing human-decisions flow.
349	- Local-model layer (`src/worker/local_model.py`) talks to vLLM / Ollama
350	  endpoints on the user's GPU hosts (`snorlax` RTX 4090, `may` RTX 3090)
351	  via OpenAI-compatible HTTP. Numbered-slot env config
352	  (`KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_<n>_*`), priority ordering, a TTL-cached probe, and
353	  a `KCA_LOCAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` cloud fallback.
354	- New job types `log_triage` and `summarise` route to the local layer by
355	  default; `kca local probe / pick / triage` surfaces endpoint state.
356	- OTEL instrumentation per ADR-0007 with three exporters: stderr (dev),
357	  SQLite (`.agent/telemetry.sqlite`), and Supabase
358	  (`agent_telemetry_spans`). Spans cover job / turn / tool / reviewer /
359	  local-probe.
360	- TC-3 Spaceship Titanic exercises the reviewer-gate path end-to-end on a
361	  binary-classification submission flow.
362	
363	Exit criteria: all met. See `docs/m6-final-review.md`.

366	
367	## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done
368	
369	_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._
370	
371	Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
372	has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
373	`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.
374	
375	This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
376	and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.
377	
378	See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.
379	
380	### Four-layer model
381	
382	| Layer | Description |
383	|---|---|
384	| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
385	| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
386	| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
387	| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |
388	
389	### M7 task sequence
390	
391	| Task | Description | Depends on |
392	|---|---|---|
393	| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
394	| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
395	| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
396	| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
397	| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
398	| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
399	| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
400	| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
401	| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
402	| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
403	| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |
404	
405	### Permission policy design
406	
407	Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:
408	
409	```json
410	{
411	  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
412	  "default_decision": "ask",
413	  "reason": "External competition submission",
414	  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
415	  "audit_required": true
416	}
417	```
418	
419	Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
420	summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.
421	
422	Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
423	remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
424	change competition direction/objective.
425	
426	Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
427	drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.
428	
429	### Recommended directory layout
430	
431	```text
432	.kca/
433	  skills/
434	    run-milestone/SKILL.md
435	    triage-log/SKILL.md
436	    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
437	    review-pr/SKILL.md
438	  tools/tools.yaml
439	  permissions/
440	    default.yaml
441	    permissive-dev.yaml
442	    competition-runner.yaml
443	
444	tools/kca/
445	  kca.py
446	  commands/
447	    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
448	    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
449	  agent/
450	    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
451	    permission_policy.py  audit.py
452	```
453	
454	Exit criteria:
455	
456	- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
457	- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
458	- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
459	- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
460	- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
461	- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
462	- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
463	- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.

```
# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-21 (M7 exit)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, and approvals.
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

## Completed milestones
- **M0**: project baseline and memory discipline ✓
- **M1**: local Kaggle tooling wrapper baseline ✓
- **M2**: Supabase/control plane foundation ✓
- **M3**: Python-first competition worker v0 ✓
- **M4**: Kaggle competition workflow v0 ✓
- **M5**: research and browser workflow ✓
- **M6**: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓
- **M7**: KCA CLI architecture (command / skill / tool / permission policy) ✓

See `docs/m7-final-review.md` for M7 validation results (28/28 checks PASS).

## Current milestone: M8 — product UI shell

Status: planned. Expose the control plane through a React/TypeScript UI (Next.js or Vite) built in Claude Code: approval inbox, run timeline, experiment table, artifact browser. M7 follow-ups (skill → worker wiring, DB audit table, tool executor integration) tracked in `docs/m7-final-review.md` § M8 follow-ups.
```

642	Goal: create four SKILL.md files under .kca/skills/.
643	
644	---  .kca/skills/run-milestone/SKILL.md  ---
645	---
646	name: run-milestone
647	description: Execute a milestone task end-to-end in an isolated workspace until acceptance criteria pass or blockers are documented.
648	version: "1.0"
649	argument-hint: "[task-md-path]"
650	arguments:
651	  - task_path
652	allowed-tools:
653	  - read_file
654	  - edit_file
655	  - write_file
656	  - bash
657	  - git_commit
658	  - gh_pr_create
659	  - run_tests
660	  - litellm_call
661	  - create_artifact
662	approval-policy: permissive-dev
663	tags:
664	  - platform-dev
665	  - milestone
666	---
667	
668	Execute milestone task `$task_path`.
669	
670	Workflow:
671	1. Read $task_path and CLAUDE.md.
672	2. Inspect the current architecture and test state.
673	3. Create or use an isolated workspace/branch.
674	4. Make the smallest coherent change that advances the acceptance criteria.
675	5. Run relevant tests, lint, type checks, and smoke tests.
676	6. Iterate until acceptance criteria pass or a decision gate is reached.
677	
678	Produce on completion:
679	- Summary of changes made.
680	- List of changed files.
681	- Test results.
682	- Risks and known regressions.
683	- Unresolved blockers.
684	- Recommended next task.
685	
686	Stop conditions:
687	- All acceptance criteria pass.
688	- A decision gate is reached (create a decision record instead of proceeding).
689	- Max turns, budget, or time is reached.
690	---
691	
692	---  .kca/skills/triage-log/SKILL.md  ---
693	---
694	name: triage-log
695	description: Summarise and classify a job's event log into actionable findings using a local or cloud LLM.
696	version: "1.0"
697	argument-hint: "[job-id]"
698	arguments:
699	  - job_id
700	allowed-tools:
701	  - read_file
702	  - litellm_call
703	approval-policy: permissive-dev
704	tags:
705	  - triage
706	  - log-analysis
707	---
708	
709	Triage agent job `$job_id`.
710	
711	Steps:
712	1. Fetch the job's event trail via `kca run logs --job-id $job_id`.
713	2. Route to a local model endpoint if available (see `kca local probe`).
714	3. Produce a structured summary:
715	   - Job status and outcome.
716	   - Key decisions made.
717	   - Errors and failures with root causes.
718	   - Recommended next action: retry / escalate / close.
719	---
720	
721	---  .kca/skills/prepare-submission/SKILL.md  ---
722	---
723	name: prepare-submission
724	description: Validate a run's submission.csv, check format and metric, and create a submission decision record ready for human approval.
725	version: "1.0"
726	argument-hint: "[run-dir]"
727	arguments:
728	  - run_dir
729	allowed-tools:
730	  - read_file
731	  - bash
732	  - create_artifact
733	  - litellm_call
734	approval-policy: default
735	tags:
736	  - kaggle
737	  - submission
738	---
739	
740	Prepare submission for run at `$run_dir`.
741	
742	Steps:
743	1. Verify submission.csv exists and header matches competition format.
744	2. Check row count and that target column values are valid.
745	3. Load metrics.json; confirm cv_score is recorded.
746	4. Summarise: run_id, competition, cv_score, submission_path, artifact_hash.
747	5. Create a decision record:
748	   `kca decision create --operation kaggle_submit --run-id <id> --reason "CV:<score>"`
749	6. Print the decision record ID. Do NOT submit — human must approve via
750	   `kca decision approve <id>`.
751	
752	Stop if:
753	- submission.csv is missing or malformed → fail with clear error.
754	- cv_score is missing → warn and stop.
755	---
756	
757	---  .kca/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md  ---
758	---
759	name: review-pr
760	description: Review a pull request for correctness, test coverage, and safety alignment with CLAUDE.md rules.
761	version: "1.0"
762	argument-hint: "[pr-number-or-branch]"
763	arguments:
764	  - pr_ref
765	allowed-tools:
766	  - read_file
767	  - bash
768	  - web_fetch
769	  - run_tests
770	  - litellm_call
771	approval-policy: permissive-dev
772	tags:
773	  - code-review
774	  - platform-dev
775	---
776	
777	Review PR or branch `$pr_ref`.
778	
779	Steps:
780	1. `gh pr diff $pr_ref` or `git diff main...$pr_ref` — collect the diff.
781	2. Read changed files in full.
782	3. Read CLAUDE.md safety boundaries.
783	4. Assess: correctness, test coverage, security, CLAUDE.md alignment.
784	5. Run tests: `python -m pytest tests/ -v -m "not db"`.
785	6. Produce a structured review:
786	   - Summary of changes.
787	   - Issues found (blocking / non-blocking).
788	   - Test results.
789	   - Security concerns.
790	   - Recommendation: approve / request-changes / needs-human-review.

809

````markdown
# M8 Loop Prompts

_Product UI shell — React/TypeScript front-end on top of the M2–M7 control plane._
_For sequential, mostly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M7 exit criteria confirmed met (see `docs/m7-final-review.md`)._

---

## M8 at a glance

M8 turns the headless KCA platform into a usable workbench by adding a human
interface on top of the M2 control plane, M5 research data, M6 reviewer /
telemetry data, and the M7 permission policy + audit trail.

M8 is **not** a greenfield UI experiment: it must respect every safety
boundary M2–M7 enforced. The Supabase client used by the UI never bypasses
the `permission_policy` resolution or the `kaggle_submit` / `kernel_push`
approval gates. The UI's job is to **render** those decisions for a human,
not to forge them.

M8 also absorbs the six follow-ups carried forward from `docs/m7-final-review.md`:

1. Wire skill execution through the worker (`kca skill run <name>` non-dry-run
   now pipes the rendered skill body into `AgentWorker` with
   `JobPolicy.approval_gates` populated from `resolve_for_skill`).
2. Promote `agent_job_events.event_type="tool_audit"` into a dedicated
   `agent_tool_audit` table + view (migration 0007).
3. JSON-Schema gate for SKILL.md frontmatter (refuse malformed skills at load).
4. Hook `ToolSpec.timeout_s`, `sandbox`, and `approval_label` into
   `src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call` so runtime matches declared policy.
5. Retire `.kca/skills/_test_fixture/` — replace with a real platform skill
   or move into `tests/fixtures/`.
6. CI: confirm secret wiring on the `live-db` job, gate forks, add a
   UI build/lint/typecheck job.

### UI layers shipped in M8

| Layer | Tech | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| **App shell** | Vite + React + TypeScript + React Router | layout, nav, auth, theming |
| **Data client** | `@supabase/supabase-js` + typed schema | read-only Supabase queries against the existing tables |
| **Action client** | small Python-FastAPI service (or direct DB writes via signed RPC) | approve/reject decisions, never the kaggle CLI itself |
| **UI primitives** | Tailwind CSS + headlessui (no design-system dep) | tables, cards, modal, toasts |
| **Charts (minimal)** | `recharts` | CV-score timeline, cost-over-time |

Pages shipped:

| Page | Source data | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | `projects`, `competitions`, `runs` | overview cards, "in-flight" runs |
| Run Timeline | `agent_job_events`, `agent_telemetry_spans` | OTEL spans from M6 rendered as a swim-lane |
| Experiments | `experiments`, `runs`, `submissions` | sortable by metric |
| Research | `research_items`, `research_citations` (M5) | trust label + source URL |
| Approval Inbox | `human_decisions`, `agent_reviews`, `agent_tool_audit` (M7 follow-up #2) | shows operation, cv_score, cost_so_far, artifact preview |
| Decision Gate | one decision detail page | Approve / Reject / Ask-agent-to-improve actions |
| Artifacts | `artifacts` + storage paths | browse, preview small files only |

DB/sandbox notes carry over from M7:

```bash
SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres
KCA_DB_TARGET=local
```

Container IP may change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
```bash
docker inspect supabase-db --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
```

DB calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`. The Vite dev server runs
inside the normal sandbox on `localhost:5173`.

---

## M8 task summary

| Task | Goal | Loop Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| M8-T000 | UI stack ADR + scaffold (Vite + React + TS, Tailwind, Supabase client) | Prompt 0 |

## Loop Prompt 0 — UI stack ADR + scaffold (M8-T000)

```
Read:
1. docs/milestones.md   (M8 section — stack constraints + planned capabilities)
2. docs/handoffs/m7-handoff.md   (M7 → M8 handoff, M7 follow-ups)
3. docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md   (the surface M8 calls into)
4. docs/adr/   (latest ADRs — match style)
5. pyproject.toml   (kca entry point + dev deps)
6. .claude/settings.json   (permissions allow-list for npm/pnpm/node/vite)

Goal: decide and document the UI stack, then scaffold the `ui/` workspace
with Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + `@supabase/supabase-js`.

Step 1 — Write docs/adr/ADR-0011-ui-stack.md.
  - Status: Accepted.
  - Context: M8 needs a TypeScript-first React surface developed in Claude
    Code, talking to the existing Supabase control plane. Two viable shapes:
      A) Next.js app router (file-based routing, RSC, API routes).
      B) Vite + React + React Router (pure SPA, no SSR).
  - Decision: **Vite + React + React Router**. Rationale:
      - The product is an operator/dev workbench, not a public site; SEO
        and SSR are non-goals.
      - Backend writes already live in `tools/kca/*` + `src/worker/`;
        the UI does not need API routes.
      - Faster cold-start dev loop matches the Claude Code editing cadence.
      - Smaller surface to keep safe with the M7 permission policy.
  - Consequences:
      - All authenticated mutations go through Supabase RPC functions or
        a small Python action service (M9+). The browser never holds a
        service-role key.
      - Server-rendered features (e.g. social previews) are explicitly
        out of scope for M8.

Step 2 — Scaffold `ui/`:
  mkdir -p ui
  cd ui
  pnpm create vite . --template react-ts
  pnpm add @supabase/supabase-js react-router-dom recharts clsx
  pnpm add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer @types/node \
    @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom vitest jsdom \
    @playwright/test
  pnpm exec tailwindcss init -p

Step 3 — Wire Tailwind + base CSS:
  - `ui/tailwind.config.js`: content `["./index.html", "./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]`.
  - `ui/src/index.css`: `@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;`
  - Replace the Vite template `App.tsx` with a placeholder
    `<h1 className="p-4 text-2xl">kaggle-code-agent</h1>` so the smoke test
    has something to assert on.

Step 4 — Supabase client stub (read-only):
  ui/src/lib/supabase.ts:
    import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
    const url  = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL  ?? "http://localhost:54321";
    const anon = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ?? "";
    export const supabase = createClient(url, anon, {
      auth: { persistSession: false },
    });

  ui/.env.example:
    VITE_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321
    VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=replace_me

  Confirm `ui/.env*` is in the repo-level `.gitignore`.

Step 5 — Wire the root package scripts:
  ui/package.json scripts: `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `test`,
  `typecheck` (= `tsc --noEmit`).

Verification:
  cd ui && pnpm install                 → 0 errors
  cd ui && pnpm typecheck               → 0 errors
  cd ui && pnpm build                   → builds to ui/dist
  cd ui && pnpm dev &                   → serves on :5173

  grep -q "Vite + React" docs/adr/ADR-0011-ui-stack.md

Do NOT git add or commit. Report: pnpm install summary, build output size,

## Loop Prompt 1 — `agent_tool_audit` migration (M8-T001)

```
Read:
1. docs/m7-final-review.md   (§ M8 follow-up #2)
2. supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql   (style template)
3. tools/kca/agent/audit.py   (AuditRecord fields + JSONL writer)
4. tools/kca/db.py            (append_job_event implementation)
5. docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md   (Audit trail section)

Goal: add a first-class `agent_tool_audit` table, backfill the M7 JSONL
records into it, and switch the audit writer to dual-write
(`JSONL` for offline ops + DB when `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is set).

Step 1 — Write supabase/migrations/0007_m8_tool_audit.sql:
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_tool_audit (
    id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    ts          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    session_id  UUID        NOT NULL,
    job_id      UUID        NULL REFERENCES agent_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    skill_name  TEXT        NULL,
    tool_name   TEXT        NOT NULL,
    operation   TEXT        NOT NULL,
    decision    TEXT        NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('allow','ask','deny')),
    mode        TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
    policy_profile TEXT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
    audit_required BOOLEAN  NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    args_hash   TEXT        NOT NULL,
    extra       JSONB       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
  );
  CREATE INDEX agent_tool_audit_session_idx ON agent_tool_audit(session_id);
  CREATE INDEX agent_tool_audit_job_idx     ON agent_tool_audit(job_id);
  CREATE INDEX agent_tool_audit_ts_idx      ON agent_tool_audit(ts DESC);

  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_agent_tool_audit_recent AS
    SELECT a.*, j.skill_name AS job_skill_name, j.status AS job_status
    FROM agent_tool_audit a
    LEFT JOIN agent_jobs j ON j.id = a.job_id
    ORDER BY a.ts DESC
    LIMIT 200;

Step 2 — Update tools/kca/db.py:
  - Add `def insert_tool_audit(rec: dict) -> None` that INSERTs into
    `agent_tool_audit`. Best-effort: if no DB, return silently.
  - Keep `append_job_event(event_type="tool_audit", ...)` working but mark
    it deprecated in a docstring.

Step 3 — Update tools/kca/agent/audit.py:
  - In `AuditLogger.record`, when `backend in ("db", "both")` AND
    `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is set, call `insert_tool_audit(rec)` in addition
    to writing the JSONL line.
  - Never raise on DB failure; log to stderr and continue.

Step 4 — Optional backfill script:
  scripts/backfill_tool_audit.py:
    - Reads .agent/audit.jsonl
    - Inserts each line into agent_tool_audit (de-dup by (session_id, ts, tool_name)).
    - Idempotent.
  Document it in docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md § Audit trail.

Verification (DB calls require dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true):
  # apply migration
  psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" -f supabase/migrations/0007_m8_tool_audit.sql
  psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" -c "\d agent_tool_audit"
    → table present with all columns

  # writer dual-writes
  python -c "
  from tools.kca.agent.audit import AuditLogger
  import pathlib, json, uuid
  log = AuditLogger(backend='both', file_path=pathlib.Path('.agent/audit.jsonl'))
  rec = log.log_policy_decision(
      tool='bash', operation='bash', decision='ask',
      skill_name='_test_fixture', mode='default',
      policy_profile='permissive-dev',
      args={'cmd': 'echo hi'},
  )
  print('wrote', rec.session_id)
  "
  psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM agent_tool_audit;"
    → at least 1

  python -m pytest tests/ -v -m "not db"   → 0 failures
  python -m pytest tests/ -v -m db         → all DB tests pass (with sandbox off)

Do NOT git add or commit. Report: migration applied, row count, JSONL still
present, deprecation note added.
```

## Loop Prompt 3 — Skill → worker wiring + `ToolSpec` enforcement (M8-T003)

```
Read:
1. src/worker/worker.py                 (_tool_call, AgentWorker loop)
2. src/worker/_types.py                 (JobPolicy, approval_gates)
3. src/worker/tools.py                  (current tool dispatch)
4. tools/kca/skill.py                   (kca skill run handler)
5. tools/kca/agent/tool_registry.py     (ToolSpec.timeout_s, sandbox, approval_label)
6. tools/kca/agent/permission_policy.py (resolve_for_skill)
7. docs/m7-final-review.md              (§ M8 follow-ups #1 and #4)

Goal: implement the M7 follow-ups #1 and #4 together — `kca skill run`
without `--dry-run` now drives an `AgentWorker` whose tool calls are
gated by the M7 permission policy and respect the ToolSpec metadata.

Step 1 — `kca skill run <name> [--mode <mode>] --execute` (or drop --dry-run
to keep the existing flag shape):
  - Build a JobPolicy:
      policy = JobPolicy(
          skill_name=name,
          allowed_tools=skill.meta.allowed_tools,
          approval_gates={
              tool: resolve_for_skill(skill.meta, tool, mode=args.mode)
              for tool in skill.meta.allowed_tools
          },
          max_turns=..., max_cost_usd=..., max_runtime_s=...,
      )
  - Create the agent_job row via tools/kca/db.create_agent_job(skill_name=name,
    policy=policy, rendered_prompt=rendered_body, …).
  - Hand to AgentWorker.run(job_id).

Step 2 — In src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call:
  - Resolve the ToolSpec via tool_registry.get_tool(tool_name).
  - Enforce ToolSpec.timeout_s as a hard timeout (use signal/alarm or
    subprocess.run timeout depending on the tool implementation).
  - Honour ToolSpec.sandbox:
      "sandboxed"          → run in current process (no extra escape).
      "unsandboxed"        → require approval_label resolved to "allow"
                             OR a satisfied approval gate from policy.
      "isolated_workspace" → cwd must be the job's workspace path.
  - Cross-check JobPolicy.approval_gates[tool_name]:
      "allow" → proceed.
      "ask"   → write human_decisions row + agent_job_events("decision_pending")
                + return a paused-job marker; do NOT execute.
      "deny"  → raise PolicyViolation, mark job failed.
  - On any decision, call audit.log_policy_decision(...) so the
    `agent_tool_audit` table records the outcome.

Step 3 — Tests:
  - Extend tests/test_m7_smoke.py (or add tests/test_m8_worker_wiring.py)
    with three tests:
      a) approval_gate "allow" → tool executes, audit row records "allow".
      b) approval_gate "ask"   → job pauses, human_decisions row created,
                                  audit row records "ask", no side effect.
      c) approval_gate "deny"  → job fails, no side effect, audit row "deny".
  - Use a fake ToolSpec ("noop_test_tool") wired into TOOL_REGISTRY behind
    a `_register_test_tool()` helper guarded by `pytest`-only import — do
    not pollute the production registry.

Verification:
  python -m pytest tests/test_m8_worker_wiring.py -v   → 3 passed
  python -m pytest tests/ -v -m "not db"                → 0 failures

  # End-to-end smoke with a benign skill (no real Kaggle / GH side effects):
  python tools/kca/kca.py skill run triage-log \
    --arg job_id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 --execute --json
    → ok=true, job_id returned, audit rows present (verify via
      `python tools/kca/kca.py tool audit --limit 3 --json`)

  # Deny path: try to run a skill whose policy resolves to deny
  # (use competition-runner profile + an op that returns deny).
  # Confirm job ends with status="failed" and human_decisions has the row.

Do NOT git add or commit. Report: 3 wiring tests, audit rows, end-to-end
smoke job ID + status.
```

## Loop Prompt 9 — Approval Inbox + Decision Gate (M8-T009)

```
Read:
1. supabase/migrations/0003_m3_worker.sql       (human_decisions)
2. supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql (agent_reviews)
3. supabase/migrations/0007_m8_tool_audit.sql   (agent_tool_audit)
4. tools/kca/decisions.py                       (approve / reject CLI)
5. tools/kca/agent/permission_policy.py         (decision semantics)
6. docs/milestones.md   (M8 § Decision-gate UI requirements)

Goal: the most important M8 page. A human sees every pending decision,
approves / rejects / asks-the-agent-to-improve, and the write path goes
through the EXISTING `kca decisions` mechanism — the browser never
bypasses the permission policy.

Step 1 — `ui/src/pages/ApprovalInbox.tsx`:
  - List human_decisions where status = 'pending'.
  - Columns: operation, run_id link, requested_at, policy_profile,
    reviewer_verdict (from agent_reviews if any), action link.
  - Default sort: oldest first ("FIFO so nothing rots").

Step 2 — `ui/src/pages/DecisionGate.tsx` (route /approvals/:id):
  Show the full context required by the milestone spec:
    - operation
    - cv_score (joined from runs.metric_value where metric_name='cv_score')
    - cost_so_far (joined from agent_jobs.cost_so_far)
    - artifact preview (top 50 lines if the file is text and < 1 MB;
      otherwise a download link only — never preview binaries inline)
    - reviewer verdict + reasoning (from agent_reviews)
    - recent tool audit entries for the job (from agent_tool_audit)

  Three actions:
    - Approve  → POST to action service (Step 3) with reason field optional.
    - Reject   → POST with reason required (UI enforces minLength=8).
    - Ask agent to improve → POST with a structured "feedback" payload
      (free text + optional metric_target). The backend appends to
      `agent_job_events` and resumes the job at the next planning turn.

  All three actions disable buttons immediately and show a spinner until
  the response comes back. On success, redirect to /approvals.

Step 3 — Action service:
  Stand up a tiny FastAPI app at `services/decision_api/` (Python).
    POST /decision/:id/approve
    POST /decision/:id/reject
    POST /decision/:id/ask-improve
  Each endpoint:
    - Validates the user (M8 ships local-only: simple HMAC over
      `KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN`; UI reads token from a same-origin
      cookie set out-of-band by `kca ui login`).
    - Calls the existing functions in tools/kca/decisions.py.
    - Writes audit via tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision.
  Wire pnpm dev's vite.config.ts to proxy `/api/*` to localhost:8787.

UI rules:
  - The browser cannot construct a `kaggle competitions submit` call; it
    can only call /decision/:id/approve. The actual submit still flows
    through the worker after the approval is recorded.
  - "Approve" button is RED-DESTRUCTIVE-style if the operation is
    SUBMISSION-class (kaggle_submit, kernel_push, supabase_migrate),
    AMBER-CAUTION-style otherwise.
  - Decision changes are atomic: the API rejects with 409 if the
    decision is already non-pending.

Verification:
  cd ui && pnpm test -- --run                   → DecisionGate tests assert
    button colour by operation class + the "minimum 8 chars" reason rule.

  # Action service round-trip (offline; the API is mocked to not call
  # real Kaggle):
  python -m pytest services/decision_api/tests -v   → all pass

  # Manual smoke:
  KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN=dev-token \
    uvicorn services.decision_api.app:app --port 8787 &
  cd ui && pnpm dev &
  curl -s http://localhost:5173/approvals | grep -q "Approval Inbox"
  pkill -f "vite|uvicorn" || true

  cd ui && pnpm typecheck                       → 0 errors
  python -m pytest tests/ -v -m "not db"        → 0 failures

Do NOT git add or commit. Report: 3 actions, 409 atomic rule, button
colour rules, all tests green.
```

## Loop Prompt 13 — M8 architecture documentation (M8-T013)

```
Read:
1. docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md   (style template)
2. ui/src/lib/db.ts                            (data flow inventory)
3. services/decision_api/app.py                (action service shape)
4. supabase/migrations/0007_m8_tool_audit.sql  (audit table)

Goal: write docs/architecture/m8-ui-shell.md.

Required sections:

## Overview
One paragraph: M8 surfaces the M2–M7 control plane as a read-mostly UI.
The browser never writes to Supabase directly except through the
decision_api action service, which routes through the existing
`tools/kca/decisions.py` paths so M7 policy gates stay authoritative.

## Layer map
Diagram (ASCII) of:
  Browser (Vite SPA) → Supabase JS (read) → Postgres
                    → /api/decision/* → decision_api → kca decisions → Postgres
                                                                       → worker resume

## Data flow per page
For each of: Dashboard, RunTimeline, Experiments, Research, ApprovalInbox,
DecisionGate, Artifacts — list the tables read and the joins performed.

## Auth model
- Local-only token via KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN.
- M8 ships single-user; multi-user lands in M9 or later.
- No service-role key ever reaches the browser.

## Approval gate semantics
- "Approve" / "Reject" / "Ask agent to improve" map to existing
  `tools/kca/decisions.py` functions.
- The browser cannot mutate `agent_jobs.status` directly; only the
  action service can, and only via the kca decisions API.
- M7 permission_policy.resolve_for_skill is the source of truth for
  which operations need a decision; UI is purely a presentation layer.

## Audit trail
- Every action service mutation writes a row to `agent_tool_audit`.
- `.agent/audit.jsonl` continues to exist for offline ops; the dual-write
  behaviour from M8-T001 keeps both backends in sync when DB is available.

## Adding a new page
Step-by-step: add route → add typed query in `ui/src/lib/db.ts` →
add page component → write vitest test → optional Playwright case.

## Adding a new approve-class operation
Step-by-step: add ToolSpec to TOOL_REGISTRY (M7) → add policy record →
add decision_api wiring → render in DecisionGate.
````

```
28	    tool_name: str

40	def _hash_args(args: dict | None) -> str:
41	    if not args:
42	        return ""
43	    try:
44	        serialized = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True, default=str)
45	    except TypeError:
46	        serialized = str(sorted(args.items()))
47	    return hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

54	class AuditLogger:
55	    backend: str = "file"  # "file" | "db" | "both"
56	    file_path: Path = field(default_factory=_default_audit_path)
57	    db_available: bool = False
58	    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: _SESSION_ID)
59	
60	    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
61	        try:
62	            self.file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
63	        except OSError as exc:
64	            sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] mkdir failed: {exc}\n")
65	
66	    def record(self, rec: AuditRecord) -> None:
67	        if self.backend in ("file", "both"):
68	            self._ensure_dir()
69	            try:
70	                with self.file_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
71	                    fh.write(json.dumps(rec.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
72	            except OSError as exc:
73	                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] write failed: {exc}\n")
74	
75	        if self.backend in ("db", "both") and self.db_available:
76	            try:
77	                from db import append_job_event  # type: ignore
78	
79	                append_job_event(
80	                    job_id=str(uuid.UUID(int=0)),
81	                    event_type="tool_audit",
82	                    event_data=rec.to_dict(),
83	                )
84	            except Exception as exc:
85	                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] db append failed: {exc}\n")
86

88	        self,
89	        *,
90	        tool: str,
91	        operation: str,
92	        decision: str,
93	        skill_name: str | None = None,
94	        mode: str = "default",
95	        policy_profile: str = "default",
96	        args: dict | None = None,
97	        audit_required: bool = False,
98	    ) -> AuditRecord:
99	        rec = AuditRecord(
100	            timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
101	            session_id=self.session_id,
102	            skill_name=skill_name,
103	            tool_name=tool,
104	            operation=operation,
105	            decision=decision,
106	            mode=mode,
107	            policy_profile=policy_profile,
108	            audit_required=audit_required,
109	            args_hash=_hash_args(args),
110	        )
111	        self.record(rec)
112	        return rec
```

```
386	    params: list[Any] = []
387	    if competition_slug:
388	        query = query.format(where="where er.run_dir like %s")
389	        params.append(f"runs/{competition_slug}/%")
390	    else:
391	        query = query.format(where="")
392	    params.append(limit)
393	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
394	        cur.execute(query, params)
395	        rows = cur.fetchall()
396	    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

400	    run_dir: str,
401	    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,

407	def _find_run_by_dir(conn: "psycopg.Connection", run_dir: str) -> dict | None:
408	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
409	        cur.execute(
410	            """
411	            select
412	              er.id::text         as experiment_run_id,
413	              er.external_run_id  as run_id,
414	              er.run_dir,
415	              e.id::text          as experiment_id
416	            from experiment_runs er
417	            join experiments e on e.id = er.experiment_id
418	            where er.run_dir = %s
419	            order by er.created_at desc
420	            limit 1
421	            """,
422	            (run_dir,),
423	        )
424	        row = cur.fetchone()
425	    return dict(row) if row else None

555	def _create_job(
556	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
557	    project_id: str,
558	    prompt: str,
559	    policy: dict,
560	    model: str,
561	    competition_slug: str | None,
562	    session_id: str | None,
563	) -> str:
564	    competition_id = None
565	    if competition_slug:
566	        with conn.cursor() as cur:
567	            cur.execute(
568	                "SELECT id::text FROM competitions WHERE slug = %s LIMIT 1",
569	                (competition_slug,),
570	            )
571	            row = cur.fetchone()
572	            if row:
573	                competition_id = row["id"]
574	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
575	        cur.execute(
576	            """
577	            INSERT INTO agent_jobs
578	              (project_id, session_id, competition_id, status, payload,
579	               prompt, model, policy)
580	            VALUES
581	              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, 'queued', %s::jsonb,
582	               %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
583	            RETURNING id::text
584	            """,
585	            (
586	                project_id,
587	                session_id,
588	                competition_id,
589	                json.dumps(policy),
590	                prompt,
591	                model,
592	                json.dumps(policy),
593	            ),
594	        )
595	        row = cur.fetchone()
596	    conn.commit()
597	    assert row is not None
598	    return row["id"]

618	def lease_job(
619	    job_id: str,
620	    worker_id: str,
621	    lease_seconds: int = 300,
622	    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
623	) -> bool:
624	    """Atomically set status='running', leased_by, leased_until.
625	
626	    Returns True if successfully leased, False if already running/leased.
627	    """
628	    return _with_conn(conn, _lease_job, job_id, worker_id, lease_seconds)
629	
630	
631	def _lease_job(
632	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
633	    job_id: str,
634	    worker_id: str,
635	    lease_seconds: int,
636	) -> bool:
637	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
638	        cur.execute(
639	            """
640	            UPDATE agent_jobs
641	               SET status = 'running',
642	                   leased_by = %s,
643	                   leased_until = now() + (%s || ' seconds')::interval,
644	                   started_at = COALESCE(started_at, now())
645	             WHERE id = %s::uuid
646	               AND status IN ('queued', 'paused')
647	            """,
648	            (worker_id, str(lease_seconds), job_id),
649	        )
650	        updated = cur.rowcount
651	    conn.commit()
652	    return updated > 0

967	def _create_experiment_m4(
968	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
969	    competition_id: str,
970	    hypothesis: str,
971	    job_id: str | None,
972	    branch: str | None,
973	    config: dict,
974	) -> str:
975	    # The M1 experiments table requires project_id + name; the M4 INSERT must
976	    # populate them as well so both schema shapes coexist on the same row.
977	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
978	        cur.execute(
979	            "SELECT project_id::text FROM competitions WHERE id = %s::uuid",
980	            (competition_id,),
981	        )
982	        comp_row = cur.fetchone()
983	        project_id = (comp_row or {}).get("project_id") or DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID
984	        synth_name = (branch or hypothesis or "m4-experiment")[:120]
985	        cur.execute(
986	            """
987	            INSERT INTO experiments
988	              (project_id, name, competition_id, job_id, hypothesis, branch, config)
989	            VALUES
990	              (%s::uuid, %s, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
991	            RETURNING id::text
992	            """,
993	            (
994	                project_id,
995	                synth_name,
996	                competition_id,
997	                job_id,
998	                hypothesis,
999	                branch,
1000	                json.dumps(config),
1001	            ),
1002	        )
1003	        row = cur.fetchone()
1004	    conn.commit()
1005	    assert row is not None
1006	    return row["id"]

1194	) -> list[dict]:
1195	    if experiment_id is not None:
1196	        query = (
1197	            "SELECT * FROM experiment_runs WHERE experiment_id = %s::uuid "
1198	            "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
1199	        )

1203	            "SELECT er.* FROM experiment_runs er "

1208	        params = [competition_id, limit]
1209	    else:
1210	        query = "SELECT * FROM experiment_runs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
1211	        params = [limit]
1212	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
1213	        cur.execute(query, params)
1214	        rows = cur.fetchall()
1215	    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

1780	def record_span(
1781	    *,
1782	    trace_id: str,
1783	    span_id: str,
1784	    parent_span_id: str | None = None,
1785	    job_id: str | None = None,
1786	    kind: str,
1787	    name: str,

1789	    ended_at=None,
1790	    duration_ms: int | None = None,

1792	    status: str = "ok",
1793	    error: str | None = None,
1794	    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
1795	) -> int:
1796	    """Insert one agent_telemetry_spans row. Best-effort: never raises.
1797	
1798	    Returns the new span row id, or -1 if the DB is unreachable.
1799	    """
1800	    try:
1801	        return _with_conn(
1802	            conn,
1803	            _record_span,

1805	            span_id,
1806	            parent_span_id,
1807	            job_id,
1808	            kind,
1809	            name,

1811	            ended_at,
1812	            duration_ms,
1813	            attributes or {},
1814	            status,
1815	            error,
1816	        )
1817	    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - best-effort exporter
1818	        import sys
1819

1824	def _record_span(
1825	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
1826	    trace_id: str,
1827	    span_id: str,
1828	    parent_span_id: str | None,
1829	    job_id: str | None,
1830	    kind: str,
1831	    name: str,
1832	    started_at,
1833	    ended_at,
1834	    duration_ms: int | None,
1835	    attributes: dict,
1836	    status: str,
1837	    error: str | None,
1838	) -> int:
1839	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
1840	        cur.execute(
1841	            """
1842	            INSERT INTO agent_telemetry_spans
1843	              (trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, job_id, kind, name,
1844	               started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, attributes, status, error)
1845	            VALUES
1846	              (%s, %s, %s, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb, %s, %s)
1847	            RETURNING id
1848	            """,
1849	            (
1850	                trace_id,
1851	                span_id,
1852	                parent_span_id,
1853	                job_id,
1854	                kind,
1855	                name,
1856	                started_at,
1857	                ended_at,
1858	                duration_ms,
1859	                json.dumps(attributes),
1860	                status,
1861	                error,
1862	            ),
1863	        )
1864	        row = cur.fetchone()
1865	    conn.commit()
1866	    assert row is not None
1867	    return row["id"]

1945	def _with_conn(conn, fn, *args, **kwargs):
1946	    """Call fn(conn, *args) using the provided conn or a freshly opened one.
1947	
1948	    When this function opens the connection, it also closes it.
1949	    """
1950	    if conn is not None:
1951	        return fn(conn, *args, **kwargs)
1952	    c = get_conn()
1953	    try:
1954	        return fn(c, *args, **kwargs)
1955	    finally:
1956	        c.close()
```
